answer: An agent marketplace weights votes by escrowed stake, with each unit counted once across all identities and locked for 30 days after voting. Its registration inlet accepts new accounts freely, but a comet of fresh aliases brings no extra voting power: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still yields only 100 votes. The market offers no haven for cheap sybil influence; an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital to gain more control.
